framework.notes: references/patterns.md and references/python.md were loaded. No framework reference file matched (django.md/flask.md/fastapi.md are inapplicable: the project is an ORM library with no HTTP layer), so source/sink shapes were derived from repository code per the WORKFLOW.md no-framework-match rule. The ORM's public query-builder API (Table.raw, WhereRaw, OrderByRaw, where/limit/offset/order_by/as_of/values/on_conflict delegates, Column comparison operators) is the trust boundary through which an embedding application's (potentially attacker-controlled) values enter SQL construction, and is modeled as the api_param source family. The QueryString class itself is the parameterized-query core: it keeps {} placeholders and args separate, and engines compile to $1/? bound parameters (querystring.py:163-192) - values passed as QueryString args are the SAFE channel, values interpolated into the template string (f-strings) are the unsafe channel.

inputBoundaryInventory.summary: The project is an ORM library, so its external-input surface differs from a web app: (1) NO HTTP/API request surface exists in library code (documented absent, not fabricated); (2) the `piccolo` CLI (targ) maps argv onto plain function parameters - ~61 module-level functions under piccolo/apps/*/commands/ (fixture load path, migration app_name/migration_id, schema generate schema_name, user create/change_password/change_permissions username/admin flags, tester pytest_args, project/app new names...); (3) 12 interactive input() prompts (migration backwards/clean confirmations, schema_differ rename confirmations with an auto_input bypass, user create username/email/password/flags, asgi new router/server choices); (4) sys.argv reads in main.py; (5) os.environ: PICCOLO_CONF module resolution (conf/apps.py:365), tester env manipulation, sql_shell subprocess env copy - operator-level trust; (6) file input: fixtures load (open(path).read() -> load_json -> pydantic validation -> parameterized INSERTs), migration files executed via MigrationManager; (7) DB content: table reflection (TableStorage.reflect) and schema generation read table/column/constraint names from information_schema via parameterized raw queries, and those names are re-interpolated into DDL f-strings (intermediate propagation, not external input); (8) the library's public ORM API, through which the embedding application passes values (modeled as api_param). The dominant SQL execution channel is engine-layer: asyncpg connection.fetch/execute/cursor and aiosqlite connection.execute, all fed by QueryString.compile_string() output; the unsafe channel is f-string/concat template construction (LIMIT/OFFSET/AS OF/ORDER BY delegates, engine SAVEPOINT/BEGIN/ROWID statements, ALTER DDL statements, Raw/WhereRaw/OrderByRaw template arguments).

sinkInventory.summary: The final SQL execution layer is entirely inside piccolo/engine/: asyncpg connection.fetch(query, *args) / connection.execute(statement) / connection.cursor(template, *template_args) for Postgres+Cockroach, and aiosqlite connection.execute(query, args) / cursor.execute(statement) for SQLite. Everything above it is SQL construction: QueryString templates (parameterized {} placeholders compiled to $n/? bound parameters), DDL string assembly (f-strings in alter.py/create.py), and engine-internal statement f-strings (SAVEPOINT/BEGIN/ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT/PRAGMA/ROWID lookup). The dangerous sink modeling target is the SQL text argument (positional index 0) of the execution calls; the bound-parameter channels (asyncpg *args after the query, aiosqlite execute(query, args) argument 1) are extracted separately so parameterized calls are distinguishable from text injection.

safeChannelNotes: QueryString.compile_string (querystring.py:163-192) keeps args out of the SQL text: postgres/cockroach get $1..$n placeholders, sqlite gets ? placeholders - values passed as QueryString args are bound parameters, NOT SQL text

Where values, insert row values, fixture data, user-admin values all ride the bound-args channel; the bound_params sink family records this channel separately so parameterized calls are not flagged as text injection
QueryString.__str__ (querystring.py:93-122) interpolates values into a display string via template.format - it is documentation/debug output, never executed; it is deliberately NOT a sink family

extractionQueries.sources: iris/extraction/sources.ql - 10-column contract identical to the arches/django runs: node, role('source_candidate'), callable, flow_kind, receiver, moduleHint, arg_index, file, line, match_kind
extractionQueries.executionMode: codeql query run + codeql bqrs decode (NOT database analyze / SARIF); plain multi-column select queries with no @kind problem metadata - a problem-shaped query is the wrong shape for candidate tables and no @kind table is assumed to exist

uncoveredCases: LazyLoader dynamic imports: asyncpg/aiosqlite are assigned to local names at import time (postgres.py:15, sqlite.py:21, cockroach.py:10), so API-graph resolution of connection.fetch/execute/cursor to library APIs is impossible; ALL sink rows are AST-level (match_kind 'ast') and receiver-name-based, with receiver-collision noise left to labeling

Method-name-based ORM API matching: api_param/internal_transfer families match (enclosing class name, method name) pairs; subclass overrides, monkey-patching, and dynamic dispatch through self.* proxies (e.g. FrozenQuery.__getattr__) are not traced

Keyword-argument transfers (e.g. Savepoint(name=...), OnConflictItem(target=...), SetColumnType(using_expression=...)) are not captured by the positional internal_transfer family; dataclass __init__s (OrderByRaw.sql, SetColumnType.using_expression, Readable.template) are generated code with no AST parameter node - they are only observable at their consumption sites (SQL-producing functions)

targ CLI registration is not resolved: command functions are approximated by file path (piccolo/apps/*/commands/*.py, module-level functions); helpers defined in the same files are included as candidates

Cross-function SQL assembly: strings built in one function and passed to QueryString/execute in another (select.py default_querystrings query += ...) are captured only at the final construction point (dynamic_sql_template) and via construction nodes inside SQL-producing function names (default_querystrings, *_querystrings, ddl, *_ddl, _get_joins); other intermediate assignments are not tracked at extraction time (taint tracking in Phase 2 handles propagation)

DB reflection results (TableStorage.tables, RowMeta fields in schema generate) enter SQL construction as schema names; the schema_name family captures the read points (_meta.tablename / _meta.db_column_name / get_formatted_tablename()) but no taint step from reflection queries to those names is modeled yet
JsonOperator / call_chain SQL fragments in column_types.py and select.py build column-path strings dynamically; only the f-string construction nodes inside SQL-producing functions capture them
